Check a design and its schema before anything is selected or written

Source: R/design.R
validate_design.Rd

run_pipeline() calls this right after reading the two files, so a design that cannot be honoured is refused before any output exists, with the same message in both engines. It first refuses a key within one or two edits of a key lexsync reads at that level, naming the key it was probably meant to be (one edit for a known key of up to five characters, two for a longer one). It then refuses a missing, empty or non-text name or language, an n_per_condition, n_per_cell or resample.n_sets that is not a whole number of at least 1, a counterbalance.optimise that is not true or false, a counterbalance.scale other than mean or mad, a counterbalance.max_run or counterbalance.orders that is not a whole number of at least 1, and a counterbalance.run_on that is not the name of a column. It refuses a name, language or font that cannot be written into the generated experiments, a trigger port that is not an address, and an event list the renderer refuses, such as one with an unknown timing key, a bad response key or a response key that YAML reads as a boolean (an unquoted yes, no, on or off). It refuses a presentation.fullscreen that is not true or false and a presentation.text_height_px that is not a whole number from 8 to 400. It refuses a triggers.mode other than auto, hardware or mock, a triggers.backend other than parallel or serial, and a triggers.baudrate that is not a positive whole number. A serial backend needs a triggers.serial_port, with a name the experiments can carry. Last, it refuses a condition without a name, with a name that is not text or with a repeated name, a corpus or pool design with conditions but no match_on, and a name and language that leave no file stem. It also refuses an exclude_words that is neither a list of words nor a mapping whose path names a file, and one that a design with an item table names.

Usage

validate_design(design, schema)

Arguments

design

A parsed design configuration.

schema

The parsed global schema.

Value

A character vector of notes on unknown keys, in the order the keys were written, then the note on triggers.inter_trigger_ms; empty when there are none.

Details

Any other key lexsync does not read is not refused yet. It is returned as a note, which run_pipeline() writes into the run log, and a later release will refuse it. description and keys beginning x_ are annotations and are never noted. A schema that still sets triggers.inter_trigger_ms, which no longer does anything, gets a note too.

The experiments' instructions and response mapping are checked here too. It refuses instructions that are not text, are empty or hold a control character other than a line break. It refuses a response_mapping that is not a mapping of conditions to single keys, names a key the response event does not allow, or comes with no response event. And it refuses a rotate_mapping_by_list that is not true or false, or that has no mapping to rotate.

Examples

validate_design(list(name = "demo", language = "english", x_note = "pilot"), list())
#> character(0)
